ai.description: This skink reaches 8 cm snout-vent length. It is brown with a dark lateral band containing white spots. A pale dorsolateral stripe and smooth, overlapping scales are diagnostic.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Sphenomorphus maculatus* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous dark brown lateral stripe bordered by a pale dorsolateral line, unlike similar species.
ai.habitat: The Spotted Forest Skink inhabits leaf litter in moist deciduous and evergreen forests, typically ranging from lowlands up to 1,500 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Spotted Forest Skink is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates among leaf litter and rocky outcrops during the sunlit hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sphenomorphus maculatus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Sphenomorphus maculatus* occurs in Northeast India, primarily within the Eastern Himalayas and Assam, ranging from lowlands up to approximately 1,500 meters in elevation.
